sentences.en: all this stuff as early as 1984.
sentences.zh: 早在1984年就已经开始阐述这些观点了。

sentences.en: He certainly understood at an early stage what the internet was going to do for communication.
sentences.zh: 他在早期就敏锐地理解了互联网将为通信带来的变革。

sentences.en: But there was a flip side to Dowlin's visionary concept of digitally networked libraries.
sentences.zh: 但道林关于数字化网络图书馆的构想也有其另一面。

sentences.en: Some people felt that Dowlin had a distressing lack of concern for books.
sentences.zh: 有些人觉得道林对书籍有一种令人痛心的冷漠。

sentences.en: There was this sense that when it came to the physical collections, he just didn't have any
sentences.zh: 人们有一种感觉，当涉及到实体藏书时，他根本没有任何

sentences.en: Dowlin was also overseeing the design of a new main library for the city of San Francisco,
sentences.zh: 道林还负责监督旧金山市新总图书馆的设计工作，

sentences.en: which would complete his vision of the library of the future.
sentences.zh: 这将完善他对未来图书馆的愿景。

sentences.en: The city is building a new $100 million library that is wired for computers as well as television.
sentences.zh: 这座城市正在建造一座耗资1亿美元的新图书馆，里面铺设了电脑和电视线路。

sentences.en: This new library would have twice as much space as the old one, but a big chunk of that space
sentences.zh: 这座新图书馆的空间将是旧图书馆的两倍，但其中的很大一部分空间

sentences.en: wasn't going to be for shelving books.
sentences.zh: 并不打算用来摆放书架。

sentences.en: Instead, much of the library's interior was devoted to an atrium in the middle of the building,
sentences.zh: 相反，图书馆内部的大部分空间都用于建筑中央的中庭，

sentences.en: which would rise 86 feet to a conical glass roof.
sentences.zh: 该中庭向上延伸86英尺，直达一个圆锥形的玻璃屋顶。

sentences.en: Lots of librarians worried that this big, empty atrium wouldn't leave a lot of space for books.
sentences.zh: 许多图书管理员担心，这个巨大而空旷的中庭留给藏书的空间并不多。

sentences.en: The atrium was evidence that books were not the sole priority of this building,
sentences.zh: 这个中庭证明了书籍并不是这座建筑唯一的首要任务，

sentences.en: and Dowlin wasn't going to let a good crisis go to waste.
sentences.zh: 而道林是不会白白浪费一场好危机的。

sentences.en: The earthquake was a perfect excuse to do what he wanted to do anyway,
sentences.zh: 地震为他做他一直想做的事提供了完美的借口，

sentences.en: shrink the physical collection before the move to the new space.
sentences.zh: 那就是在搬进新空间之前缩减实体藏书的规模。

sentences.en: Dowlin's administration started sending books to landfills.
sentences.zh: 道林的行政团队开始将书籍运往垃圾填埋场。

sentences.en: In the days after the quake, books are being sent out by the truckload several times a week.
sentences.zh: 地震发生后的几天里，卡车满载着书籍每周运出好几次。

sentences.en: This is not normal library practice.
sentences.zh: 这不是正常的图书馆运作惯例。

sentences.en: Twenty-seven librarians signed a petition asking Kenneth Dowlin for the weeding to stop,
sentences.zh: 27名图书管理员签署了一份请愿书，要求肯尼斯·道林停止清理工作，

sentences.en: So Jason Gibbs and his colleagues decided to do something.
sentences.zh: 于是杰森·吉布斯和他的同事们决定采取行动。

sentences.en: In any institution, you have a variety of people.
sentences.zh: 在任何机构里，你都会遇到形形色色的人。

sentences.en: There are some people who will just kind of do whatever they're told,
sentences.zh: 有些人只会按吩咐行事，

sentences.en: and then there are other people who feel like they have a higher calling to the profession.
sentences.zh: 而另一些人则觉得他们对这个行业有着更高的使命感。

sentences.en: Gibbs and librarians from several other departments felt that higher calling.
sentences.zh: 吉布斯和其他几个部门的图书管理员感受到了这种更高的使命感。

sentences.en: They banded together and called themselves the guerrilla librarians.
sentences.zh: 他们联合起来，自称游击队图书管理员。
像自由战士一样的游击队员。

sentences.en: Fighting for the freedom to not put little slips of red paper on books against the orders of management.
sentences.zh: 为了反抗管理层的命令、捍卫不在书上贴红色小纸条的自由而战。

sentences.en: Let's just say that we did not withdraw books because they hadn't circulated.
sentences.zh: 我们只想说，我们撤下书籍并不是因为它们没有被借阅过。

sentences.en: We generally held on to the collection.
sentences.zh: 我们通常都把这些藏书保留了下来。

sentences.en: Jason says that other guerrilla librarians snuck into the stacks and replaced red slips with green ones,
sentences.zh: 杰森说，其他游击队图书管理员偷偷溜进书库，用绿色的纸条替换了红色的纸条，

sentences.en: thereby designating the book as a circulating book and keeping it in the collection.
sentences.zh: 从而将这些书指定为可流通书籍并将其保留在藏书中。

sentences.en: The guerrilla librarians wanted to determine exactly how many books had been weeded and how many had been dumped.
sentences.zh: 游击队图书管理员想要弄清楚到底有多少书被清理了，多少书被丢弃了。

sentences.en: But nobody had any idea how many books were being taken away.
sentences.zh: 但没有人知道到底有多少书被运走了。

sentences.en: And there was a risk that they'd never be able to find out the magnitude of this massive clearing.
sentences.zh: 并且存在这样一种风险，即他们永远无法查明这次大规模清理行动的严重程度。

sentences.en: Because Kenneth Dallin decided to get rid of the physical card catalog.
sentences.zh: 因为肯尼斯·道林决定扔掉实体卡片目录。

sentences.en: Those files full of index cards chronicling each book.
sentences.zh: 那些记录着每一本书的索引卡片的档案柜。

sentences.en: The card catalog is an artifact.
sentences.zh: 卡片目录是一个时代的产物。

sentences.en: But I will not support the view that the card catalog is a working technology to help people find books anymore.
sentences.zh: 但我不再支持卡片目录作为一种帮助人们寻找书籍的有效技术的观点。

sentences.en: And most of the libraries in the world know that and have moved on.
sentences.zh: 世界上大多数图书馆都意识到了这一点，并已经向前迈进。

sentences.en: Already at that point, more than 90% of the nation's libraries had computerized their card catalogs.
sentences.zh: 早在那个时候，全国90%以上的图书馆就已经将卡片目录电脑化了。

sentences.en: The earthquake itself allowed the San Francisco Public Library to modernize their catalog.
sentences.zh: 地震本身使旧金山公共图书馆得以将其目录现代化。

sentences.en: With the disaster relief money they were granted, the library was able to get electronic catalog software.
sentences.zh: 凭借获批的灾难救济金，该图书馆得以购置电子目录软件。

sentences.en: So now, logically, Dallin wanted to get rid of the physical card catalog, which the library had stopped updating in 1991.
sentences.zh: 因此，从逻辑上讲，道林想要摆脱实体卡片目录，该图书馆已于1991年停止更新卡片目录。

sentences.en: San Francisco's old card catalog was not moved to the new library.
sentences.zh: 旧金山旧的卡片目录并没有搬到新图书馆。

sentences.en: It is locked up and inaccessible to the public.
sentences.zh: 它被锁起来了，公众无法访问。

sentences.en: But this move to get rid of the old card catalog caused a surprisingly intense outcry from the guerrilla librarians.
sentences.zh: 但这一废除旧卡片目录的举动引发了游击队图书管理员出乎意料的强烈抗议。

sentences.en: And it wasn't just a matter of nostalgia or personal preference.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是怀旧或个人喜好的问题。

sentences.en: The physical card catalog said exactly what was in the library before all the arbitrary weeding.
sentences.zh: 实体卡片目录准确记录了在所有随性清理之前图书馆里到底有什么书。

sentences.en: If a book was red-tagged and weeded, it wouldn't be registered in the new digital system.
sentences.zh: 如果一本书被贴上红签并清理掉，它就不会登记在新的数字系统中。

sentences.en: There would be no record it had ever existed at all.
sentences.zh: 将没有任何记录表明它曾存在过。

sentences.en: And so the old card catalog was more than just a card catalog.
sentences.zh: 因此，旧卡片目录不仅仅是一份卡片目录。

sentences.en: To get to the card catalog, the librarians pulled out their secret weapon.
sentences.zh: 为了触及卡片目录，图书管理员们拿出了他们的秘密武器。

sentences.en: I'm Nicholson Baker, and I am a writer of books, fiction, nonfiction.
sentences.zh: 我是尼科尔森·贝克，我是一名书籍、小说和非虚构作品作家。

sentences.en: And I became, for a brief period of time, a library activiSt.
sentences.zh: 在很短的一段时间里，我成为了一名图书馆维权人士。

sentences.en: Baker is a writer of novels and essays that celebrate the minutiae of daily life.
sentences.zh: 贝克是一位小说家和散文家，其作品赞美日常生活中的细枝末节。

sentences.en: And in 1994, Baker had gotten national attention for a New Yorker article about the disposal of physical card catalogs,
sentences.zh: 1994年，贝克因《纽约客》上一篇关于处理实体卡片目录的文章而受到全国关注，

sentences.en: a practice that had become increasingly common and which upset Baker a lot.
sentences.zh: 这种做法变得越来越普遍，这让贝克非常难过。

sentences.en: The San Francisco Public Library had a very ornate, beautiful card catalog.
sentences.zh: 旧金山公共图书馆拥有一个非常华丽、精美的卡片目录。

sentences.en: That feeling that you have when your fingers would dance over the little cardboard pieces,
sentences.zh: 当你用手指在小纸板上轻快滑动时，那种感觉，

sentences.en: and you could tell a subject that was popular because the tops were darker.
sentences.zh: 你可以通过顶部较深颜色的磨损程度来判断某个主题是否受欢迎。

sentences.en: There's all sorts of, you know, tricks that were just fun.
sentences.zh: 这里面有各种各样的小技巧，你知道的，都很有趣。

sentences.en: The guerrilla librarians reached out to Baker for help.
sentences.zh: 游击队图书管理员向贝克寻求帮助。

sentences.en: By now, it was 1996, and the new library was nearing completion.
sentences.zh: 此时已是1996年，新图书馆即将完工。

sentences.en: The lost books, evidenced only by their locked-away card catalog, were teetering on the edge of disregard.
sentences.zh: 那些遗失的书籍，仅凭其被锁起来的卡片目录证明其存在，正处于被忽视的边缘。

sentences.en: In their email to Nicholson Baker, the librarians wrote,
sentences.zh: 图书管理员在给尼科尔森·贝克的电子邮件中写道，

sentences.en: You are the only one who can save it now.
sentences.zh: 现在只有你能拯救它了。

sentences.en: Part of me thought, oh God, this is going to get complicated.
sentences.zh: 我心里的一部分想，天哪，这下可要复杂了。

sentences.en: At the time, Baker was living just across the bay in Berkeley.
sentences.zh: 当时，贝克住在海湾对岸的伯克利。

sentences.en: So he made a formal request to inspect the card catalog.
sentences.zh: 因此，他正式提出查阅卡片目录的请求。
肯尼斯·道林拒绝了这一请求。

sentences.en: So Baker sued the library for access to the card catalog.
sentences.zh: 于是贝克起诉了图书馆，要求获得查阅卡片目录的权利。

sentences.en: Never sue anything if you can avoid it, and don't sue a library.
sentences.zh: 能避免就不要起诉任何东西，更不要起诉图书馆。

sentences.en: This lawsuit took a while, and it was a bit of a mess.
sentences.zh: 这场诉讼持续了一段时间，而且有点一团糟。

sentences.en: But it automatically classified the card catalog as a public document.
sentences.zh: 但它自动将卡片目录归类为公开文件。

sentences.en: Now the library had to keep it.
sentences.zh: 现在图书馆必须保留它。

sentences.en: And then Baker and the guerrilla librarians got to work in secret.
sentences.zh: 接着，贝克和游击队图书管理员们秘密地开始了工作。

sentences.en: And, you know, you can imagine this with kind of Mission Impossible music going.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，你可以想象伴随着《碟中谍》的音乐，发生这一切。

sentences.en: The guerrilla librarians snuck into off-limits areas in the library.
sentences.zh: 游击队图书管理员偷偷溜进了图书馆里的禁区。

sentences.en: They took away books that were going to be destroyed.
sentences.zh: 他们带走了那些即将被销毁的书籍。

sentences.en: In other words, they stole them.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他们偷走了它们。

sentences.en: The guerrillas stockpiled hundreds and hundreds of library discards.
sentences.zh: 游击队员们囤积了成百上千本被图书馆丢弃的书籍。

sentences.en: In their homes, in their cars, in their offices, in lockers, in boxes.
sentences.zh: 放在家里、车里、办公室里、储物柜里、箱子里。

sentences.en: All in the hope that they would someday be returned to the library.
sentences.zh: 这一切都怀揣着有一天它们能重返图书馆的希望。
尼科尔森·贝克也偷了书。

sentences.en: I was driving back and forth across the Bay Bridge with my car full of books
sentences.zh: 我开车在海湾大桥两头来回奔波，车里装满了书，

sentences.en: that I had actually found in this place that was the deselection room.
sentences.zh: 这些书实际上是我在一个被称为淘汰室的地方发现的。

sentences.en: Baker ignored the staff-only signs and walked right into the deselection room,
sentences.zh: 贝克无视“员工专用”的标志，径直走进了淘汰室，

sentences.en: the basement storage, all the places where the SFPL were storing books.
sentences.zh: 地下室仓库，以及旧金山公共图书馆存放书籍的所有地方。

sentences.en: He picked up a bunch of books that had no match in the online catalog
sentences.zh: 他挑出了一堆在在线目录中找不到匹配项的书籍，
并发现了一些真正的珍宝。

sentences.en: They had stored all these, you know, including 17th century,
sentences.zh: 他们把所有这些都存放在那里，你知道的，包括17世纪的藏书，

sentences.en: very valuable books and stuff was down there.
sentences.zh: 非常珍贵的书籍和其他东西都在那里。

sentences.en: Baker, along with a historian, began comparing the online catalog
sentences.zh: 贝克与一位历史学家一起，开始比对在线目录

sentences.en: As they cross-referenced the two lists,
sentences.zh: 当他们交叉核对这两份名单时，

sentences.en: it turned out that a lot of books were missing.
sentences.zh: 结果发现有很多书不见了。

sentences.en: Way more than anyone had expected.
sentences.zh: 比任何人预期的都要多得多。

sentences.en: Let me tell you, what an opening day celebration today.
sentences.zh: 不瞒你说，今天的开馆庆典真是盛大。

sentences.en: At last, in April of 1996, the new main library opened its doors, with panache.
sentences.zh: 终于，在1996年4月，全新的总图书馆隆重开馆。

sentences.en: Nothing less than a parachute jump into Civic Center
sentences.zh: 甚至有人直接跳伞空降到市民中心，

sentences.en: with the man holding the symbolic key to the new library.
sentences.zh: 手里还拿着象征新图书馆大门的钥匙。

sentences.en: And in May of 1996, about a month after the library opened,
sentences.zh: 而在1996年5月，也就是图书馆开馆大约一个月后，

sentences.en: the guerrilla librarians organized an event in the library auditorium,
sentences.zh: 这群“游击队员”式的图书馆员在图书馆礼堂组织了一场活动，

sentences.en: where Baker delivered a speech stating what he had found.
sentences.zh: 贝克在会上发表了演讲，公布了他的发现。

sentences.en: Baker contended that Dowlin was responsible for a massive destruction of books,
sentences.zh: 贝克断言，道林应对大规模的毁书行为负责，

sentences.en: the systematic removal to a landfill of at least 200,000 volumes.
sentences.zh: 即系统性地将至少20万册图书运往垃圾填埋场丢弃。

sentences.en: And I just said it right there in the library itself, in a talk,
sentences.zh: 我当时就在图书馆的演讲中直言不讳地指出了这一点，

sentences.en: and I think it really startled people.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这确实让大家震惊了。

sentences.en: The phrase that got Baker the most attention
sentences.zh: 让贝克受到最多关注的那句话是，

sentences.en: was when he called this mass disposal, a quote,
sentences.zh: 他将这种大规模的销毁行动称为——引述原话——

sentences.en: hate crime directed at the paSt.

sentences.zh: 这让图书馆管理层非常恼火。

sentences.en: And it became this kind of minor dust-up in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 这成了旧金山一场不小的风波。

sentences.en: Word had begun to spread that Baker was writing another story for the New Yorker,
sentences.zh: 有消息开始传出，贝克正在为《纽约客》撰写另一篇文章，

sentences.en: one specifically about this whole weeding debacle.
sentences.zh: 专门讲述这场轰轰烈烈的图书清理风波。

sentences.en: So the president of the Library Commission
sentences.zh: 于是图书馆委员会主席

sentences.en: wrote to the New Yorker's editor at that time
sentences.zh: 写信给当时的《纽约客》主编，

sentences.en: and attempted to kill the piece by discrediting Baker.
sentences.zh: 企图通过抹黑贝克来扼杀这篇文章。

sentences.en: It didn't work, and Baker's article came out in October of 1996.
sentences.zh: 但这没有得逞，贝克的文章最终于1996年10月发表了。

sentences.en: It was called The Author vs. the Library.
sentences.zh: 文章名为《作家对决图书馆》。

sentences.en: A current New Yorker article called it the Great Book Purge,
sentences.zh: 《纽约客》最近的一篇文章称之为“大藏书清洗”，

sentences.en: claiming more than 100,000 rare and one-of-a-kind books were hauled to the dump.
sentences.zh: 声称有超过10万册珍稀和绝版图书被运到了垃圾场。

sentences.en: And then things got a little out of hand.
sentences.zh: 然后事情就有点失控了。

sentences.en: The library hit back, condemning Baker for accusing them of a hate crime
sentences.zh: 图书馆发起反击，谴责贝克指责他们犯下了仇恨犯罪，

sentences.en: and saying that he misunderstood the problem.
sentences.zh: 并称他误解了这个问题。

sentences.en: They also tried to discredit him because of some bad math he had reported.
sentences.zh: 他们还试图利用他报告的一些错误数据来诋毁他。

sentences.en: It turns out, one of the guerrilla librarians
sentences.zh: 原来，其中一位“游击派”馆员

sentences.en: had messed up the measurements of the old library shelves.
sentences.zh: 搞错了旧图书馆书架的尺寸测量数据。

sentences.en: In fact, the new library had much more space for books than the old one.
sentences.zh: 事实上，新图书馆存放图书的空间比旧图书馆大得多。

sentences.en: It was a very bad error.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常严重的错误。

sentences.en: Although it didn't change the fact that the library had taken so many books to the dump.
sentences.zh: 尽管这并没有改变图书馆运走了大量图书的事实。

sentences.en: Then both sides started lobbying insults at each other
sentences.zh: 随后，随着当地和全国媒体的纷纷加入，

sentences.en: as the local and national press piled on.
sentences.zh: 双方开始互相抛出侮辱性言论。

sentences.en: One paper compared Baker to the Unabomber.
sentences.zh: 有一家报纸甚至把贝克比作大学航空炸弹狂人。

sentences.en: It was basically an analog Twitter feud.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是一场模拟的推特骂战。

sentences.en: I wasn't prepared to be part of it.
sentences.zh: 我并没有准备好卷入其中。

sentences.en: I didn't know that I was getting into that kind of a battle.
sentences.zh: 我不知道自己会陷入这种争端。

sentences.en: And even from guerrilla librarian Jason Gibbs' standpoint,
sentences.zh: 甚至从“游击派”馆员杰森·吉布斯的角度来看，

sentences.en: the whole weeding controversy got a little blown out of proportion.
sentences.zh: 整场清理争议也有点被夸大了。

sentences.en: It probably was not as horrible as Nicholson Baker made it out,
sentences.zh: 它可能没有尼克尔森·贝克所描述的那般可怕，
